projectCharter.client: Industrial Transmission Systems - Mechanical Design Dept
projectCharter.projectBackground: A intermediate power transmission shaft in a heavy industrial machine tool is subjected to simultaneous transverse loading from a central drive pulley and torque transmission from a motor coupling. Overheating bearings and shaft misalignment indicate potential excessive bending deflection and high shear stresses.
projectCharter.engineeringContext: As a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer, management has assigned you to analyze the loading on the shaft, calculate bearing reaction forces, maximum bending moment, transmitted torque, determine equivalent twisting moment per ASME design code, compute minimum required shaft diameter, verify actual shear stress against allowable strength, and render a safety decision.
objectives: Identify key elements of the power transmission shaft assembly.
Understand combined bending and torsional loading mechanisms.
Formulate design requirements and record engineering assumptions.
Calculate bearing reactions, maximum bending moment, and transmitted torque.
Use the Shaft Design Calculator to determine required shaft diameter (ASME Code).
Check actual shear stress and Factor of Safety for the selected diameter.
Render a justified Safe/Unsafe engineering decision and technical recommendations.
deliverables: Free Body Diagram & Load Analysis Calculations
projectCharter.professionalResponsibility: Failure to accurately account for combined bending and torsional stresses leads to sudden shaft fatigue failure, keyway shearing, or bearing destruction.
projectCharter.safetyConsiderations: The shaft must operate within allowable shear stress limits under keyway stress concentration conditions with an adequate Factor of Safety.
projectCharter.acceptanceCriteria: Complete all 10 engineering activities with verified mathematical calculations, calculator integration, and technical justifications.

project-charter.title: Project Charter

cards.title: Real-World Industrial Scenario
cards.body: In the heavy machine manufacturing division of Kirloskar Engineering, Pune, an industrial lathe headstock drive shaft transmits 15 kW power at 720 rpm from an electric motor via a central V-belt drive pulley. The shaft is supported by two self-aligning pillow block ball bearings spaced 500 mm apart and delivers output torque to the main gearbox through a flexible coupling. The combined tension from the belt drive applies a downward transverse radial force of 3000 N at the middle of the bearing span. Recent maintenance logs report excessive shaft deflection and elevated bearing temperature under full-load operation. As a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer, you are assigned to evaluate the combined bending and torsional stress state, determine the required shaft diameter per ASME code, and verify whether the current 40 mm shaft diameter provides a safe Factor of Safety.

cards.title: Role & Assignment Scope
cards.body: As a Mechanical Design Engineer, you must analyze combined loading, determine required shaft diameter per ASME code, select standard stock diameter, evaluate shear stresses and FOS, and recommend design improvements.

engineering-context.title: Engineering Context

cards.title: Power Transmission Shaft Applications
cards.body: Shafts are rotating machine elements used to transmit mechanical power and torque between power sources (motors, engines) and driven components (pulleys, gears, pumps).

cards.title: Combined Loading Complexity
cards.body: In real machinery, shafts rarely experience pure torsion. Transverse loads from belt drives, gear teeth, or pulleys induce bending moments simultaneously with torsional loads.

engineering-context.acceptanceText: I understand the engineering context of shaft design under combined loading.

design-requirements.title: Design Requirements
given: Transverse Radial Load (F_R): 3000 N at center
Shaft Material: Plain Carbon Steel 40C8 (Syt = 380 MPa, Sut = 580 MPa)
Keyway Condition: Sunk Keyway Present (25% reduction in allowable stress)

engineering-assumptions.title: Engineering Assumptions
engineering-assumptions.prompt: Record essential engineering assumptions for static shaft design under combined bending and torsion.
questions: 1. State assumptions regarding shaft material properties (homogeneity, isotropy, elastic limit).
2. State assumptions regarding bearing supports (simple supports, zero moment resistance).
3. State assumptions regarding stress concentration effects caused by the keyway.

free-body-diagram.title: Free Body Diagram & Load Analysis
free-body-diagram.description: Shaft loading diagram showing bearing reaction forces R_A and R_B, central radial load F_R = 3000 N, bearing span L = 500 mm, and transmitted torque T.
given: Transmitted Power P = 15 kW, Speed N = 720 rpm
Central Load F_R = 3000 N, Span L = 500 mm
Formulas: Torque T = (60 * 10^6 * P) / (2 * pi * N) N-mm
Formulas: Max Bending Moment M = (F_R * L) / 4 N-mm
free-body-diagram.expectedProcess: Reactions R_A = R_B = 1500 N. Max Bending Moment M = 375,000 N-mm. Transmitted Torque T = 198,944 N-mm.

shaft-design-calculation.title: Shaft Design Calculation
given: Bending Moment M = 375,000 N-mm, Torque T = 198,944 N-mm
ASME Allowable Shear Stress = 0.75 * min(0.30 Syt, 0.18 Sut) = 0.75 * min(114, 104.4) = 78.3 MPa
shaft-design-calculation.expectedProcess: Te = 596,447 N-mm. tau_allow = 78.3 MPa. d_req = 33.86 mm. Standard shaft d_std = 40 mm.

material-safety-decision.title: Material, Safety & Engineering Decision
options: SAFE — Selected shaft diameter d = 40 mm provides adequate strength and acceptable shear stress (tau_act = 47.46 MPa <= 78.3 MPa).
UNSAFE — Selected shaft diameter is insufficient and exceeds allowable stress limits.
material-safety-decision.prompt: Evaluate the actual shear stress and Factor of Safety for the selected 40 mm shaft. Provide detailed engineering justification for your safety decision.

design-recommendation.title: Design Recommendation & Technical Report
questions: 1. What geometric modifications (e.g., shoulder fillet radius, keyway profile) do you recommend to reduce stress concentration at stepped shaft sections?
2. Synthesize your final engineering recommendations for manufacturing tolerances, key selection, and bearing shoulder details into a complete technical report.
